source.title: Induction Signatures Are Not Enough: A Matched-Compute Study of Load-Bearing Structure in In-Context Learning

page_placements.theme: Conditions and limits of induction-style copying (token rarity, configuration, long repeats, divergence, direction)
Interventions on induction heads and the token-index ICL score in small and mid-size models

record.file_problem: not stated; the supplied text appears to contain the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Measures induction-like copy attention and tests the effects of training data variants and targeted head ablations on few-shot ICL, but does not reproduce the original training-time measurements.
record.gate_note: The study measures final-checkpoint copy telemetry, few-shot task performance and ablation effects. It does not report training-time induction formation or a training-loss bump, nor loss by token index. Results cited from other studies are not recorded as rows. Detailed standard-benchmark scores, span-length and mix-ratio sweeps, robustness checks, and held-out perplexity are omitted from rows because the 60-row limit is used for induction/anti-induction telemetry, function-probe composites and ablations. The Figure 3 and Figure 4 score values are not transcribed numerically in the text; their rows therefore use figure-only values and the text’s descriptions.
record.test_reason: Pretrains 0.13B–1B decoder-only models on natural text with or without synthetic copy snippets under matched compute. It measures induction-head attention telemetry at the final checkpoint, 10-shot function-probe ICL, and the effect of ablating top induction-scoring heads versus random heads. These results bear on universality across sizes (V4), dependence on training data (V5) and whether few-shot task learning runs mainly through induction heads (V6). The models are not attention-only, two-head composition is not tested, and there is no training-time or token-index loss data, so V1, V2, V3 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Bi-Induct amplifies induction signatures but does not consistently improve few-shot ICL, and the 1B natural-only model is best on function probes. One correction: the relative ablation drop is largest for natural-only models at every size (−22.6%, −14.6%, −19.5%), not only at 1B. The authors conclude that eliciting a mechanism is not the same as making it load-bearing, and that backward-copy training does not raise anti-induction scores.
record.recipe_differences: Uses iso-FLOP pretraining with linearly annealed synthetic forward-copy, backward-copy or balanced snippets in a custom decoder-only model; measures final-checkpoint copy telemetry and few-shot task behavior. It does not reproduce the original training-time loss and token-index ICL measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size changes relative induction-peak timing and spread: Bi-Induct peaks are earlier at 0.13B and 0.5B, while baseline peaks first and is higher/broader at 1B. Curriculum also changes function-probe performance; the 1B natural-only model is strongest. Shot count and evaluation rule are discussed as robustness checks but their values are omitted from the rows.

fits_no_version.finding: Backward-copy (anti-induction) attention stays near zero at all sizes, even when training explicitly on backward-copy snippets. Peaks are at most about 0.04.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformers readily form forward induction heads but not backward-copy (anti-induction) heads, even when the training data contains backward copies.

fits_no_version.finding: Synthetic copy curricula strengthen or broaden induction signatures, but ablating top induction heads hurts ICL less than in natural-only models, at every size (e.g. −22.6% natural-only vs −4.9% Induction curriculum at 0.13B).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: How strong induction-head telemetry is does not predict how much a model relies on those heads; data-induced induction heads can be redundant.

record.problems: Mechanistic analysis is at the final checkpoint only, so formation timing and training-loss dynamics are unavailable. Models reach only 1B and use one architecture. Copy telemetry is an attention-alignment signature, not a direct test of two-head composition. Ablation tests top-2% heads against random heads but does not identify or ablate alternative mechanisms. Figure telemetry values are not numerically provided in the text. Ablation percentage changes have no reported uncertainty in Table 3.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted standard LM benchmark composite rows, the detailed per-task results, 1-shot and HITS@3 robustness results, span-length and mix-ratio sweeps, and held-out perplexity rows to stay within 60 rows; these are in Sections 5.1, 5.3 and Appendices C, D and E. Per-layer figure-only telemetry values were not split into individual layer rows because the plotted values are not numerically stated in the text.

untested.parts: All of it. The models are full transformers with MLPs, not attention-only, and only single-head attention alignment is measured; composition with a previous-token head is not tested.
All of it. Analysis is final-checkpoint only; there is no formation timing, loss bump or concurrent ICL gain.
All of it. There is no measurement of loss by token index, and ablations measure few-shot function-probe accuracy only.
Other model families, architectures and modalities. Only one Mistral-like decoder at three sizes is tested.
When induction heads form during training. Data properties other than injecting synthetic copy snippets into The Pile.
Which alternative heads or mechanisms carry the remaining few-shot accuracy; ablation removes only one head per layer.
All of it; no formation time course is measured.

missing.what: Mix-ratio sweep at 0.13B. Heads above the 0.5 specialization threshold: baseline 2; Induction 3/3/1, Balanced 4/4/1 and Anti 3/1/2 at 25/50/100% initial mix ratio. Specialized heads sit deeper as the mix ratio rises.
Peak induction score close to 1.0 at 0.13B and 0.5B but well below 0.5 at 1B, in all conditions.
Standard LM benchmark 3-shot composite largely unchanged by curricula (e.g. 22.7 vs 22.5 at 0.13B, 24.2 vs 24.3 at 1B).
Clean, induction-ablated and random-ablated per-task scores, e.g. 1B baseline 'choose first of 3' falls from 69.4 to 49.2 when induction heads are ablated.

record.verdict_notes: 'Top 2% per layer' with a floor of one head selects one head per layer (12–24 heads per layer), so ablations remove 12–30 heads in total. 'Earlier emergence' refers to layer depth at the final checkpoint, not training time. V1 was removed from all rows because the models are not attention-only and composition is not measured. Function-probe composites without ablation were relinked to V5 only. The accuracy drop under curricula at 1B may partly reflect displaced natural text, as the authors acknowledge.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures single-head attention alignment on copy probes, not composition with an earlier previous-token head, nor the complete two-head circuit. Models are not attention-only.
No training-time checkpoints or loss-curve measurements are reported; emergence timing, abruptness and coincidence with an ICL gain are not tested.

The study tests function-probe and standard few-shot task performance and ablates top-scoring heads, but does not measure loss falling with token index or establish what accounts for most ICL in large transformers. Its models are at most 1B parameters.

Copy signatures are evaluated at three sizes within one custom decoder-only architecture. Other model families, training runs beyond the reported seeds, other architectures and modalities are not tested.

Tests natural-only versus forward-copy, backward-copy and balanced synthetic-data curricula under the stated training recipe. It does not systematically vary natural corpora, objectives or architectures.
The study compares induction-head ablation with random-head ablation on function probes, but does not identify or ablate alternative mechanisms to determine what carries most few-shot task learning.
No formation time course is measured, so separate sub-steps or overlapping transitions are not tested.

reader_labels.condition: Natural-only versus forward, backward and balanced synthetic-copy curricula
reader_labels.reason: Curricula shift induction telemetry by scale, but do not consistently improve function-probe ICL; explicit backward-copy training does not materially increase anti-induction scores (R01-R36).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope

reader_labels.reason: Top induction-head removal is more damaging than matched random removal in the reported comparisons, indicating a causal contribution, although the study does not compare against specific alternative circuits (R37-R60).
